newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Telecom signs GSM deal with U.S. partners.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Telecom signs GSM deal with U.S. partners.

text.p: Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST), the Slovak state-owned telecom monopoly, on Friday said it had signed a Global System for Mobile (GSM) agreement with its two U.S. partners after more than four months of negotiations.

Under the agreement, the three will create a joint-stock company, Eurotel Bratislava a.s., in which ST will hold 60 percent and the two U.S. telecom groups -- U.S. West Media Group Inc and Bell Atlantic Corp -- will share the remaining 40 percent.
The conclusion of the protracted negotiations came just 11 days before a final deadline for talks as set by the Slovak Ministry of Telecommunications.

"We have just signed the agreement on creation of Eurotel Bratislava a.s. which will operate the second Slovak GSM network," Lubomir Stancel, ST spokesman told Reuters shortly after the signing ceremony.

Negotiations over the country's second GSM operator have dragged on since July, when the three partners agreed to create a new company, but had to reach a final framework for the venture conforming to the government's 60 percent Slovak ownership condition.
The talks concentrated mainly on executive rights in the new company and the split of investments.

The three companies already operate the country's sole mobile telephone network, the NMT system, through joint-venture Eurotel s.r.o., in which ST holds 51 percent and the two U.S. telecom groups together hold 49 percent.
On September 4, the telecommunications ministry formally granted one of the two planned GSM licences to Eurotel s.r.o..
But it warned the three they could lose the GSM licence if they failed to conform to the tender conditions by the deadline, 90 days after the licence was granted.
Stancel said the new company will be completely independent and that the only thing in common with Eurotel s.r.o. are its owners.

A second Slovak GSM network will be operated by Slovtel GSM a.s., a consortium of four Slovak energy companies, the state monopoly gas distributor and a private firm Hanco sro, which teamed up with France Telecom.
Slovtel announced earlier this month that it had already started to build the technical network for the GSM system.

Slovtel has pledged that it would meet the tender conditions, which stipulate that the system must be functiong in the three largest Slovak cities -- Bratislava, Banska Bystrica and Kosice -- by the end of the year.
Eurotel has so far not made public its stage of preparedness to launch GSM operations.
